10 discarded prior notions on books & reading

1. "comparison is the thief of joy"

nature is aristocratic. benchmark urself to the best that humanity has produced (only a few great men/women per century), not ur neighbor, not random ppl on social.

what ur mostly seeing is fake and only part of a person...biographies/history show u, like the Tom Wolfe title, "A Man In Full."

2. "read quietly"

I say "trade quietly" a lot these days...keep all that shit to urself, anything social or external only introduces cognitive errors and biases.

same precept goes for reading, if ur reading to impress other people or to hit some random target ("50 books per year / 500 pages per day") ur prob reading for the wrong reasons

related:

3. read the same books over and over (every 5 years?)

books are to help u navigate life. sometimes a great day of reading might just be 5 pages, but where it set ur mind in motion, shifted ur worldview or led to a change in ur behavior

that's why u "read quietly"...who cares if u only read 5 pages of a book that u already read before. no one elses opinion matters

4. more than one at a time

theres nothing wrong with reading 5-10 books at once bc sometimes u just arent in the mood, or there's a light/heavy scale, some require more focused attention than others.

if u only do one, u may feel compelled to blast thru it and not retain anything just to get to another

5. some books or authors dont "click"

there are some authors that I seem to have a "mental block" with. I've read prob 4 dostoevsky books but dont remember a thing and found it painful from start to finish. meanwhile I've read tolstoy's War and Peace twice  and could easily go back for a 3rd

another one is dickens, I've never been able to get into a single one

I just don't care, I'll try back in 5 years but I'm fine with reality being that my mind just doesnt perfectly align with some authors...we're all unique in that regard

6. how books change your circle

imo two things change a man - books and experience

sometimes the combo of the two, will cause u to re-evaluate ur own beliefs, and u will recognize that u are surrounded by the wrong people...doesnt mean theyre wrong, just a misalignment between u and them

or that u no longer agree w/ a former mentor

thats all fine...walk ur own path. books are the best "north star" u will ever have

7. the best source of books to read is books that ur reading

most book recs are best found in books

example: munger always carried "a benjamin franklin" biography with him

if a bio tells u "napoleon took this plutarch book with him on his march to moscow" i'd add that book to ur list

if montaigne praises seneca and epicurus, i'd add those to your list

if lord chesterfield frequently quotes la rochefoucauld, i'd go there next

etc etc.  these are better signposts than asking Grok

8. why do old books survive

make sure u have a firm grip on why old books survive across generations

the sandstorm of history is powerful and obsolete or archaic books get buried very fast. I bet 99.9% of "the best books of 2026" have disappeared by 2126.

so when u see a book from 500-1000 years ago that is still relevant, i'd default to "there's probably something in here that is eternal about human nature" and rank it above something published yday

9. pace

a lot of the best books, whether old books, history or bios, can be thick

great biographies easily run 800+ pages

do not feel like there's a rush. knocking out 50 pages of a biography in a day requires pretty focused attention

so if TR's bio takes you 3 months, so be it. this is still a far better use of ur time than almost anything else.

10. no twtr on weekends

this is the only way to keep ur sanity and to get any reading done, the weekdays are just too hectic for the most part

turn this shit off, the ROI is zero and probably negative

if u dont have the discipline to obey a simple rule like "no twtr on weekends" that is actually a pretty serious problem....bc it means u wont have the discipline for much much bigger shit when the time comes.

--
